title: Flat transport squares for the formal comparison
statement: Let $Y,S$ be Noetherian schemes, $f:X\to Y$ proper, $g:S\to Y$ flat, and $J,I$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves on $Y,S$ with $J.\operatorname{comap}(g)=I$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-pc-module-pullback]. Put $Z=X\times_Y S$ with $q:Z\to X$, $p:Z\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix an adjunction $a:f^*\dashv f_*$, a coherent formal $J$-system $G$, coherent $F$ on $X$, $\beta:G\mathbin\circ f^*\simeq F^\wedge$, and coherence of $H=f_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, pqf-def-coherent]. Fix $\kappa:H^\wedge\to F^\wedge\mathbin\circ f_*$ satisfying $\pi^J_n\kappa_n=f_*(\pi^{J.\operatorname{comap}(f)}_n)$ for all $n\geq0$, where $\pi_n$ denotes the quotient by the $(n+1)$st power. Suppose $G_0\in\operatorname{Coh}(S,I)$ and coherent $F_0$ on $Z$ are supplied, together with $h_G:G_0=G\mathbin\circ g^*$, $F_0=q^*F$, and coherence of $D=p_*F_0$. Then there exist $a_R:p^*\dashv p_*$, $\beta_0:G_0\mathbin\circ p^*\simeq F_0^\wedge$, $\kappa_0:D^\wedge\to F_0^\wedge\mathbin\circ p_*$, $\delta:D^\wedge\simeq H^\wedge\mathbin\circ g^*$, and $t:(F^\wedge\mathbin\circ f_*)\mathbin\circ g^*\to F_0^\wedge\mathbin\circ p_*$ such that: (1) $\pi^I_n\kappa_{0,n}=p_*(\pi^{I.\operatorname{comap}(p)}_n)$ for all $n$; (2) $\delta\,(g^*\kappa)\,t=\kappa_0$ as natural transformations; (3) for every $n$, $\operatorname{eqToHom}(h_G)_n\,g^*(\eta^a_{G_n}f_*(\beta_n))\,t_n=\eta^{a_R}_{G_{0,n}}p_*(\beta_{0,n})$. No map $\alpha:G\to H^\wedge$ or its transport is assumed or constructed.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary flat quotient-mate theorem with I replaced by J.comap g and the supplied equality eliminated. This gives adjR, beta zero, an ordinary base-change isomorphism b, a system map t, the quotient projection equation for b and t, and the adjunction-unit equation.

Apply the normalized completion-pullback theorem to g, J, the coherent pushforward f_*F, and the module (g^*f_*F), using the reflexive ideal and module equalities. Compose the completion map induced by b with the inverse of its normalized pullback isomorphism to obtain delta.

Define kappa zero as delta followed by the pulled-back kappa and t. Its transport equation is definitional. At each level, the quotient projection of the completion map induced by b is b followed by the target projection; the normalized pullback equation identifies that target projection followed by the inverse normalized pullback isomorphism with pulled-back source projection. Reassociate, use functoriality of pullback, the supplied h_kappa equation, and the ordinary quotient equation from the mate theorem. The adjunction square is the mate equation from the first step.
